sections.h2: Where to file a deed in Jackson County
sections.html:
Go upstairs to the third floor. The Recorder sits inside the courthouse at 226 East Main Street, Jackson, OH 45640, phone (740) 286-1919, fax (740) 286-8835. Counter service runs weekdays from 8:30 am to 4:00 pm, with a midday closure from 11:30 am to 12:30 pm. Time your visit around that hour.

You can pay with cash, a check or a debit or credit card. Cards add a $2.00 service fee. The county's official records begin in 1997. Anything older must be viewed and printed at the office, while later records are searchable online after you set up an account.

Deeds, mortgages, leases, affidavits and most other recordable papers are priced the same way: $39.00 covers two pages, then $8.00 for each additional page. Each printed side counts as a page. The state fixes the price. One half is the recording fee itself, and the other half is sent to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund.

Jackson County Recorder fees
Paper or serviceFee
Deed, mortgage or lease (first two pages)$39.00
Each page past two$8.00
Marginal note on a release, assignment or amendment$4.00 each
Plat or condominium drawing, each 8 by 14 sheet$40.00
UCC filing against real estate$12.00 plus $4.00 per name indexed
Uncertified copy$2.00 a page
Certified copy$2.00 a page plus $1.00 for the seal

A veteran's service discharge and one certified copy carry no fee, and a zoning resolution costs $50.00.

sections.h2: What the Auditor adds before recording
sections.html:
The Auditor's transfers page lists two charges. The conveyance fee is $4.00 per thousand, and the transfer fee is fifty cents on each parcel. The conveyance rate was raised from $1.00 per thousand of the purchase price on March 24, 1993.

The Auditor is down the hall in the same courthouse, 226 East Main Street, Suite 5, phone (740) 286-4231, open 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. Under the Auditor's Tools menu you will find a Conveyance Calculator and a Sales Reports page. R.C. 319.202(D) puts the bill on the grantor, so you carry it as the seller. Forms on the site include:

  • DTE 100, the statement of value and fee receipt in one
  • DTE 100EX, the reason an exemption applies
  • DTE 100M and 100MEX, the manufactured and mobile home versions

Sequence matters: Auditor first, Recorder second. Changing who is named on title, whether adding a person or taking one off, needs a brand new deed, which clears the Auditor before it is recorded.

sections.h2: What happens if a deed is never recorded
sections.html:
Skip the recorder and a second buyer could end up owning your house. Under R.C. 5301.25 the deed has to be recorded where the land lies. Until it is, the law treats it as fraudulent toward any later purchaser who paid in good faith.

A few things sellers often ask the Recorder:

  • Nearly every record is open to the public. Military service records go only to the veteran who earned them, with proof of ID.
  • A will is recorded through Probate Court, which charges $46.00.
  • The office suggests an attorney or other professional draft your deed.

A name error means a fresh deed, and you start again at the Auditor.

Viewing most records online starts with an account. A deed from the 1980s predates the 1997 start of the official records and has to be pulled at the courthouse itself.

To order an image, email the document's book and page to recordersoffice@jacksoncounty.us. Copies run $2.00 a page, payable by cash or check. Someone planning to list a house can also open the Sales Reports page on the Auditor's site, next to the Conveyance Calculator and a Tax Estimator.

The county's fee list reaches well past deeds. Watch for these when a title search digs up old liens or a prior owner left paperwork behind:

  • federal tax liens and other federal liens: $5.00
  • releases or partial releases of those liens: $3.00
  • a living will or health care power of attorney: $40.00
  • zoning amendments: $20.00
  • no fee for personal property tax, workers' compensation, recognizance and unemployment compensation liens, or for certificates of premium due

R.C. 317.32 and 317.36 back these charges. When an old lien turns up on your parcel, ask the Recorder which release clears it and what it costs. A release is its own filing and is not folded into the deed.

Disputes about value go to the county Board of Revision. Its members are the Auditor, the Treasurer and the President of the County Commissioners, or their designees. The board adjusts values, not tax dollars. Submit form DTE 1 to the Auditor, who serves as secretary to the board, by March 31.

Watch the details. The form needs your own opinion of value on line 8 and a notary's stamp. You generally get one complaint per three-year period, and withdrawing one still uses it up. Proof is your job, and the result can go up, go down or stay put. It will not weigh a percentage jump in the tax bill or a neighbor's lower valuation.

Questions about paying a bill go to the County Treasurer at 740-286-2402. You can pay real estate taxes online or on the Autoagent phone line, 1-844-674-1100, and skip the trip to the courthouse.

Jackson County counted 32,817 residents in July 2025 and 14,665 housing units. Owners live in 73.9% of homes. A median owner-occupied home is worth $150,700, and median household income is $57,106. The Auditor's site counts 28,916 parcels for 2024.

Have the deed drafted, preferably by an attorney. Sign it, then take it to Suite 5 to pay the conveyance and transfer fees, with form DTE 100 or the exemption form. Carry the stamped deed up to the third floor and pay the recording fee, mindful of the lunch closure. Request a copy for your files. The buyer's title company usually handles most of this at closing, so confirm who is carrying the deed to each office and by what day, and keep your receipts from both counters until the sale is fully recorded. A mortgage payoff produces a release that is recorded separately, with its own page charge and perhaps a marginal notation. Have your title company confirm it was filed. After closing, the buyer can search the new deed online, assuming it was recorded after 1997 and the buyer has set up an account. Should the recorded paper contain a mistake, call the Recorder right away.

faqs.q: How much does the Jackson County Recorder charge for a three-page deed?
faqs.a: $47.00. That is the $39.00 two-page price plus $8.00 for page three. A marginal note adds $4.00 apiece, so find out whether your paper needs any.

faqs.q: Is the Jackson County Recorder open over lunch?
faqs.a: No. It closes from 11:30 am to 12:30 pm and otherwise serves the public weekdays between 8:30 am and 4:00 pm.

faqs.q: What conveyance fee does Jackson County charge?
faqs.a: The rate is $4.00 for every thousand dollars of purchase price, with $0.50 more per parcel as a transfer fee. The $4.00 figure has applied since March 24, 1993.

faqs.q: Does paying the Jackson County Recorder by card cost extra?
faqs.a: Yes, by $2.00. That service fee applies to debit and credit cards only, not to cash or checks.

faqs.q: Does the Jackson County Recorder record wills?
faqs.a: No. A will is recorded in Probate Court, at a cost of $46.00. The Recorder files deeds, mortgages and similar land records.
